crumbs.name: Knowledge Based Professions and their Future

children.name: High-Frequency Market Microstructure
children.blurb: High-frequency market microstructure is the study of how trades actually happen at the finest timescales, from the arrival of an order to its execution or cancellation.

children.name: Non-Linear Factor Models
children.blurb: Non-linear factor models extend the linear factor framework by allowing a factor's effect on returns to depend on other factors, on the level of the factor itself, or on the market regime.

children.name: Learning Trade Execution
children.blurb: Learning trade execution is the use of machine learning to decide how, when, and where to place orders in financial markets.

children.name: Statistical Arbitrage
children.blurb: Statistical arbitrage is a quantitative trading approach that looks for relative value between related securities, often using statistical models to identify temporary mispricings.

children.name: Detecting Market Regime Shifts
children.blurb: Detecting market regime shifts is the practice of identifying when the statistical character of a market changes, for example from calm and trending to volatile and mean reverting, or from broad correlation to dispersion.

sections.body: Quantitative trading uses AI to turn market data into forecasts, execution decisions, and risk controls. In practice, models ingest order book events, trade prints, quotes, news, and alternative data to predict short horizon returns or liquidity. AI is used in market microstructure to classify order flow and estimate impact, in factor models to capture nonlinear relationships across many signals, and in execution to choose order types, venues, and timing. Statistical arbitrage systems search for relative mispricing across related instruments and close positions when signals decay. Regime shift detection tries to notice when historical relationships break, so models can reduce exposure or switch parameters. The work is mostly supervised learning, reinforcement learning, and online learning, with heavy engineering around data latency and backtest realism.
sections.heading: What this covers

sections.body: Some parts are mature. Execution algorithms and short term alpha models are widely deployed, and microstructure features are standard inputs. What is not solved includes robust out of sample performance, transaction cost estimation, overfitting, and non stationarity. Many published factor and arbitrage results weaken after costs, and regime shifts remain hard to detect before or during the break. The site tracks 117 listed AI-related instruments with daily prices, which is a useful universe for studying these issues, but daily prices alone cannot capture intraday microstructure or execution quality. Honest limits include limited historical data for rare regimes, unstable correlations, and the gap between backtest and live trading, and AI does not remove market risk or guarantee profit.
sections.heading: Where the work stands

sections.body: High-Frequency Market Microstructure is the foundation for understanding order flow, liquidity, and short horizon price formation. Non-Linear Factor Models shows how AI extends traditional factor investing by learning interactions and time varying exposures. Learning Trade Execution focuses on the action layer, where models decide how to work an order and manage market impact. Statistical Arbitrage connects signal discovery to portfolio construction and risk neutralization across related assets. Detecting Market Regime Shifts provides the monitoring layer that tells when the assumptions behind the other pages may no longer hold. A reader can start with microstructure for data and mechanics, move to factor models and stat arb for signal and portfolio ideas, then use execution and regime detection to test whether those ideas survive real trading conditions.
